Please read the technical steps before commenting or flagging. This is a reproducible architectural flaw (CWE-459), and Google’s Bug Hunter program just permanently banned me without human review to cover it up.

The Illusion of the “Delete” Button When you click “Delete permanently” in Google AI Studio, the UI explicitly warns you: “The item will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered later. This action cannot be undone.”

But that is a complete lie. The system does not send a deletion cascade to Google’s backend (Interactions API / Project Storage). All it does is move a local .json pointer file into your Google Drive Trash.

If the backend had actually purged the data, the server would return a 404. It doesn’t. The data never left their “hot storage”. The delete button is just a visual placebo.

The Cover-Up (Issue Tracker: 563791693) I submitted a full forensic dossier of this Deceptive Design to the Google VRP (Bug Hunter) program today. Here is the exact timeline:

By labeling this “Intended Behavior,” Google’s own automated triage system has put in writing that bypassing their 24-hour TTL and lying to users on the UI about permanent destruction is a deliberate corporate feature, not a bug.

I have forwarded the complete audit trail and the 106-version drive logs to the CISA and European privacy watchdogs (NOYB) for GDPR Article 17 violations.

If you think this is just a “UI glitch,” restore your own trashed JSON files and watch your “permanently deleted” sensitive data resurrect instantly.

For the full forensic breakdown, video evidence, and complete audit trail, check out my other articles on Medium: https://medium.com/@istokovicsgyorgy79
